body.statement: For every finite encoded input of size \(s\), construction of the activation truth table, quotient, all nonrepeating trace states, factor states, nested forest candidates, SUCCESS expression directed acyclic graphs of size at most \(L=o(N+1)\), and every rational binary-sink row-space certificate requires at most \(B(s)\) branches, symbols, and rational arithmetic operations; every such returned expression or slice certificate has encoding length at most \(B(s)\). This bounds the finite search space but does not assert that the unresolved global dichotomy selects a complete output on general multi-block inputs.
body.justification: A closed normal-form bound separates finite structural enumeration from the open global gluing theorem.
body.gap: Tikka et al. prove hardness and terminating sound search, while Mokhtarian et al. cover fixed root controls; neither gives this explicit endogenous-activation structural encoding bound.
body.consumer: The bound gives \(Y_0\) a serialization ceiling and a deterministic budget for the verified binary-sink module.
